failure_patterns.pattern: strength_mismatch: Selected stronger or weaker conclusions by analogy or plausibility instead of verifying every part of the stated classification.

rejected_edits.content:
**Test each option as a complete logical claim.** Make its assumptions, domain, quantifiers, and logical connectives explicit. Do not supply unstated premises (such as invariance), treat a conditional or equivalence as proving a universal assertion, or skip either direction of an if-and-only-if claim. Verify every added clause—such as a converse, counterexample, rate, uniformity, constant dependence, or local-to-global implication—separately. Apply equations relating parameters before checking endpoint, equality, strict-inequality, and otherwise cases. Compare the full conclusion clause by clause: exact asymptotics versus big-O bounds, one-sided versus two-sided estimates, exact values versus inequalities, and fixed versus parameter-dependent claims. Read limits literally: a limsup of minus infinity means the quantity eventually tends to minus infinity, whereas a liminf of minus infinity may only give a subsequence without further structure.

**Do not transfer conclusions across specialized notions.** Check the specific definition and theorem rather than importing a familiar result from a similar name. For example, distinguish a linearized solution or kernel element from an integrable deformation, and verify polynomial and characteristic-class conventions before deciding signs. Small-case checks can reveal errors but do not establish a general identity.

For PDE regularity claims, use the equation in its actual weak formulation and verify the hypotheses of the relevant regularity theorem before upgrading the solution space. Formal integration by parts through rough coefficients is not automatic: control of a matrix divergence does not give control of all coefficient derivatives, and ellipticity or VMO membership alone does not establish higher Sobolev regularity.

For named combinatorial classes, including tableau models, use the stated or standard definition exactly. Do not add, remove, or relocate an exclusion rule based on a guessed correspondence; a modified class is a distinct claim that requires support.

**Additional close-option checks.** A liminf exponent bound does not by itself guarantee an eventual lower bound with the same exponent and a fixed constant. Test conjunctions against elementary constraints; distinguish decidability from an algorithm that outputs witnesses; and distinguish only one from at most one when existence is not guaranteed.
